## Contract

**Delegator use only.** Any agent that launches subagents reads this registry to resolve compact rules, then injects matching rule text into subagent prompts under `## Project Standards (auto-resolved)`.

Subagents still read their assigned executor/phase skill. During normal runtime, they do **not** independently discover or load additional project/user `SKILL.md` files or this registry; project/user rules arrive pre-digested. Explicit fallback loading is degraded self-healing and must be reported in `skill_resolution` as `fallback-registry` or `fallback-path`.

## Selected skills and compact rules

### branch-pr

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\branch-pr\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: Create Gentle AI pull requests with issue-first checks.
- Rules:
  - Every PR MUST link an approved issue (`status:approved`) — no exceptions
  - Branch names MUST match `^(feat|fix|chore|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|revert)\/[a-z0-9._-]+$`
  - PR body MUST contain `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N` referencing the approved issue
  - PR MUST have exactly one `type:*` label matching the PR type
  - Conventional commit format: `type(scope): description` or `type: description`
  - Automated checks must pass before merge; include shellcheck for shell scripts

### chained-pr

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\chained-pr\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: PRs over 400 lines, stacked PRs, review slices.
- Rules:
  - Split PRs over 400 changed lines unless maintainer accepts `size:exception`
  - Keep each PR reviewable in ≤60 minutes
  - State start/end/prior dependencies/follow-up/out-of-scope in every chained PR
  - Every child PR must include a dependency diagram marking current PR with `📍`
  - ≤400 lines focused → single PR; >400 independent slices → Stacked PRs to main; >400 dependent → Feature Branch Chain
  - Keep tracker PR draft/no-merge until all child PRs reviewed

### cognitive-doc-design

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\cognitive-doc-design\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: Writing guides, READMEs, RFCs, onboarding, architecture, or review-facing docs.
- Rules:
  - Lead with the answer — decision/action/outcome first, context after
  - Progressive disclosure: happy path first, then details/edge cases
  - Chunk related info into small sections; keep flat lists short
  - Use headings/labels/callouts/summaries for signposting
  - Prefer tables/checklists/examples/templates over prose
  - Design for review empathy: let reviewers verify intent without reconstructing the whole story

### comment-writer

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\comment-writer\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: PR feedback, issue replies, reviews, Slack messages, GitHub comments.
- Rules:
  - Start with the actionable point; do not recap the whole PR before feedback
  - Be warm and direct like a thoughtful teammate, not a corporate bot
  - Keep to 1–3 short paragraphs or a tight bullet list
  - Explain WHY when asking for a change (give the technical reason)
  - Avoid pile-ons; comment on highest-value issue only
  - Match thread language (Spanish → Rioplatense voseo: podés, tenés, fijate)
  - No em dashes

### judgment-day

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\judgment-day\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: Judgment day, dual review, adversarial review, juzgar.
- Rules:
  - Resolve project skills before launching judges via skill registry
  - Launch two blind judges in parallel with identical target and criteria
  - Never review the code yourself; wait for both judges before synthesis
  - Classify warnings as `WARNING (real)` only if normal intended use triggers them; else downgrade to INFO
  - Ask before fixing Round 1 confirmed issues
  - Re-judge in parallel after any fix agent runs, before commit/push/done
  - Terminal states: `JUDGMENT: APPROVED` or `JUDGMENT: ESCALATED`
  - After 2 fix iterations with remaining issues, ask user whether to continue

### skill-creator

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\skill-creator\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: New skills, agent instructions, documenting AI usage patterns.
- Rules:
  - Do not create skill for trivial/one-off patterns; skill is a runtime instruction contract
  - No `Keywords` section; preserve essential trigger words in `description`
  - References must point to local files (not remote URLs)
  - Target 180–450 tokens, recommended max 700, hard max 1000
  - `description`: one physical line, YAML-safe, ≤250 chars, trigger-first
  - Frontmatter MUST include: `name`, `description`, `license`, `metadata.author`, `metadata.version`
  - Sections order: Activation Contract → Hard Rules → Decision Gates → Execution Steps → Output Contract → References

### work-unit-commits

- Path: `C:\Users\felis\.config\opencode\skills\work-unit-commits\SKILL.md`
- Trigger: Implementation, commit splitting, chained PRs, tests/docs with code.
- Rules:
  - Commit by deliverable work unit (behavior/fix/docs), NOT by file type
  - Keep tests with the code they verify; keep docs with the user-visible change
  - Each commit must tell a story — reviewer should understand why it exists from diff + message
  - Each commit should be a candidate chained PR when the change grows
  - If SDD tasks forecast >400 lines, group commits into chained PR slices before implementation
  - Verify before commit: one purpose, repo works with just this commit, rollback is reasonable
